figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Complex graphic generation from a concise user request. The examples illustrate differences in content, composition, and text rendering across generation configurations. MOSS-Image combines a pretrained diffusion transformer with prompt enhancement and optional explicit layout specifications. The proprietary output provides a visual reference; quantitative comparisons are reported in Section 5.
figures.headline: Concise-request graphics vary in content, layout and text rendering across configurations, and a plausible overall look does not ensure legible text.
citing_sentences: For such graphics, a plausible overall appearance does not guarantee legible text, complete content, or coherent spatial organization (Figure 1).

figures.caption: Overview of MOSS-Image. An intent-aware prompt enhancer constructs content and layout specifications from user requests, and a pretrained 5B single-stream DiT renders them into images through a shared text-conditioning interface. The right panel details the renderer’s joint self-attention and gated feed-forward components.
figures.headline: A prompt enhancer writes content and layout specifications that a 5B single-stream DiT renders through one shared text-conditioning interface.
citing_sentences: MOSS-Image pairs a pretrained text-and-layout generator with an intent-aware prompt enhancer (Figure 2).

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Pretraining recipe of MOSS-Image. (a) After deduplication and AI-image removal, we keep all images and caption their artifacts instead of filtering them out. (b) A ReLAION sample with its original caption, three recaptions, and layout JSON (excerpts); the JSON’s object and text boxes are drawn in orange and blue. Visible text, marked in blue, is transcribed verbatim, line breaks () included. (c) Maximum tokens per sample in each stage.
figures.headline: The recipe keeps all images and captions artifacts instead of filtering them, pairing recaptions with layout annotations.
citing_sentences: Figure 3 summarizes the recipe: corpus construction, multi-granularity and structure-aware textual supervision, and multi-stage DiT pretraining.

Bars show Bradley–Terry ratings on an Elo scale with asymptotic 95% confidence intervals. Ratings are fitted separately for the three comparison groups.
figures.headline: Human-preference Elo ratings on RLA rank the MOSS-Image backbone highest at 1807.34 among generators under shared enhanced prompts.

figures.headline: The filtered model has a higher, worse FDR6-LAION score than the unfiltered baseline at all 32 evaluated checkpoints.

figures.caption: Illustrative scene/element and summary/items conditions in normalized $yxyx$ coordinates. The examples use schematic content and coordinates. Element identifiers and parent references are removed during preprocessing; optional attributes are subject to field dropout.

citing_sentences: Figure 6 illustrates the two formats; a supplementary format appends item-level annotations to a natural-language caption.

figures.caption: Muon–AdamW maintains a convergence advantage from early to late training. Matched logit-normal runs: (a) the AdamW minus Muon–AdamW loss gap; (b) first-crossing steps at four loss targets; (c) early convergence through 500K steps; and (d) late convergence from 500K to 1.6M steps. Red lines and dots in (c,d) mark target losses and interpolated first crossings. Panels (a,b) use logarithmic step axes. Each curve represents one training run.
figures.headline: Muon–AdamW keeps a convergence advantage over AdamW from early through late training across matched runs.

figures.caption: Qualitative editing cases under layout constraints. (a) Reordering the second and third infographic steps together with their associated content. (b) Replacing KRASNOYARSK with CALIFORNIA while retaining the photograph-filled lettering style and overall composition. Within each pair, left: before; right: after. Local visual details vary.
figures.headline: Two layout-constrained edits reorder infographic steps and replace prominent lettering while keeping the overall composition.
citing_sentences: Figure 8 presents two qualitative editing cases: rearranging information blocks and replacing prominent text while retaining the overall design.

figures.label: Figure 9
figures.caption: Line-break conditioning during denoising. Top: prompt with explicit line breaks. Bottom: prompt without line breaks. Each column shows the same denoising step, progressing from left to right; labels give the step number and post-update noise level $\sigma$. Explicit line breaks help the character content of each line become recognizable earlier, with clearer text in the final displayed step.
figures.headline: With explicit line breaks, each line's characters become recognizable earlier in denoising, and the final text is clearer.
citing_sentences: Figure 9 compares the denoising process with and without explicit line breaks in the prompt.

figures.label: Figure 10
figures.caption: Generalization to a resolution unseen during training. (a) Lower-resolution comparison. (b) Relative coordinates normalized to $[0,1000]$ concentrate the content into a smaller central region at the unseen resolution. (c) Zero-centered absolute coordinates better preserve the overall spatial scale at the same unseen resolution. Images are displayed at a common height for visual comparison.
figures.headline: At an unseen resolution, relative coordinates crowd content into the center, while zero-centered absolute coordinates keep the spatial scale.
citing_sentences: Figure 10 compares a lower-resolution bee-anatomy infographic with two outputs generated at a higher resolution unseen during training, using different bounding-box coordinate representations.

abstract: Recent closed-source image generation systems can produce diverse visual content from simple compositions to information-dense graphics, yet open-weight text-to-image models still struggle with dense text and intricate layouts. To narrow this gap, we introduce MOSS-Image, an open generation system that combines high-fidelity visual synthesis with intent-aware composition. First, we pretrain a 5B single-stream diffusion transformer (DiT) from scratch with a carefully designed recipe, enabling bilingual long-form text rendering and precise layout control. Second, we develop an intention-aware agentic prompt enhancement (PE) module that translates diverse user requests into detailed content and layout specifications. Together, they enable MOSS-Image to generate text-rich and layout-coherent images. We further introduce LongLongTextBench (LLTB) for evaluating long-form English and Chinese text rendering, and RealLayoutArena (RLA) for end-to-end layout-rich generation. MOSS-Image achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-weight models on LLTB, with an average text coverage of 96.3%. On RLA, MOSS-Image ranks second in the end-to-end system comparison, while its backbone ranks first among generators evaluated with shared enhanced prompts. We will release the model, training recipe, and evaluation framework to support further research and promote the text-to-image community.

sections.body: Open-weight text-to-image models still struggle with dense text and intricate layouts. The authors split this gap into rendering and specification. They pair a 5B single-stream diffusion transformer, pretrained from scratch, with an intention-aware agentic prompt enhancer. They also introduce LongLongTextBench (LLTB) for long English and Chinese text and RealLayoutArena (RLA) for end-to-end layout-rich generation. On LLTB, MOSS-Image reaches a Mean-6 score of 96.3, against 64.9 for Qwen Image 2512. On RLA it ranks second at 1698.70 Elo, behind GPT Image 2.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Open-weight models struggle with dense text, so MOSS-Image pairs a 5B diffusion transformer with an agentic prompt enhancer.

sections.body: MOSS-Image has two parts. A prompt enhancer turns a concise request into a content and layout specification. A pretrained 5B single-stream DiT renders that specification into an image. Natural-language descriptions and structured layouts share one text-conditioning pathway, so the renderer receives both through the same interface. Section 3 covers the pretraining recipe for the renderer. Section 4 describes the inference-time enhancer.
sections.heading: System Overview
sections.headline: The system pairs a pretrained text-and-layout renderer with an enhancer that turns concise requests into specifications.

sections.body: The backbone jointly processes text tokens from a frozen Qwen3.5-9B encoder and image latents from a frozen FLUX.2 VAE. Corpus preparation removes duplicates with SSCD and removes AI-generated images, but applies no further filtering. Residual defects such as watermarks are captioned rather than excluded. Captions come from gemma4 at several granularities, and a subset has layout JSON with preserved line breaks. Training runs in three resolution stages with hybrid Muon–AdamW. In a 1B ablation, Muon reaches losses of 0.41 and 0.403 with 33.2% and 28.6% fewer steps than AdamW.
sections.heading: Pretraining Strategy
sections.headline: A 5B DiT pretrained from scratch on 3 billion deduplicated images keeps broad data and uses multi-granularity captions.

sections.body: The enhancer runs GPT-6 at inference with modular task instructions. A shared core defines constraints, the output interface and validation. Task modules add content and design guidance, selected by the requested medium. The agent retrieves knowledge and inspects reference images as needed, and adapts the specification to the target canvas. Reference images guide planning but do not directly condition the DiT. The output specifies literal text, elements, bounding boxes, typography and spatial relationships. Before rendering, it checks user constraints, completeness, layout consistency and text fit.
sections.heading: Agentic Prompt Enhancement
sections.headline: An agent routes each request to task guidance and writes structured layouts with literal text, bounding boxes and typography.

sections.body: LLTB has 240 literary-text tasks, 120 each in English and Chinese. It averages 1,339.8 characters per target, against 120.3 for LongTextBench, which the authors consider close to saturation. RLA has 61 tasks drawn from manually selected posters, infographics and user interfaces. Raters make blind pairwise comparisons, fitted as Bradley–Terry ratings on an Elo scale. For layout control, the backbone reaches a mean IoU of 0.88 on detected objects and a Layout AUC of 0.70. Ideogram 4 reaches 0.44 and 0.20 on these metrics.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: On LLTB, MOSS-Image scores 96.3 Mean-6, and on RLA it ranks second end-to-end at 1698.70 Elo.

sections.body: This section reports three qualitative observations without numbers. Modifying the layout prompt replaces content and rearranges elements while keeping the overall design. This uses text-to-image regeneration, without conditioning on the original image or extra training. Prompts with explicit line breaks let the model establish each line's characters earlier in denoising, which the authors link to better final text. Zero-centered absolute bounding-box coordinates generalize to unseen resolutions better than relative coordinates normalized to [0,1000].
sections.heading: Case Study
sections.headline: Qualitative cases report that layout prompts enable zero-shot edits, line breaks help text rendering, and zero-centered boxes transfer to unseen resolutions.

sections.body: This section points to Appendix L for the related work. That appendix groups prior work into foundation models and pretraining recipes, visual text generation, layout-conditioned generation, prompt enhancement and image agents, and evaluation of text-rich graphics. It treats Ideogram 4 as closely related concurrent work. It contrasts Qwen-Image-Agent, which operates over existing generators without training, with MOSS-Image's newly pretrained backbone and explicit layout specifications.
sections.heading: Related Works
sections.headline: Related work covers foundation models, visual text generation, layout conditioning, prompt agents and text-rich evaluation.

sections.body: The current backbone supports text-to-image generation only. It does not condition directly on reference images or support image editing. Extending it to these tasks and to iterative design refinement is future work under the current computational budget. The prompt enhancer depends on external language models. Their limitations in aesthetic judgment, reference interpretation and factual errors can lower specification quality even when rendering is faithful.
sections.heading: Limitations
sections.headline: The backbone cannot condition on reference images or edit images, and the enhancer's errors can reduce specification quality.

sections.body: The paper presents MOSS-Image as an open complex graphic generation system built on a 5B diffusion transformer pretrained from scratch. Its training combines broad image-text data, multi-granularity and structure-aware supervision, and multi-stage resolution training. The agentic enhancer translates concise requests into detailed specifications. LLTB and RLA evaluate rendering and complete-system performance. Prompt-strategy and shared-prompt comparisons complement them. The authors conclude that combining a capable renderer with explicit generation specifications supports complex graphics.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: A capable renderer combined with explicit generation specifications supports complex graphics, according to the LLTB and RLA results.

sections.body: Appendix A gives the model configuration, the frozen Qwen3.5-9B encoder and FLUX.2 VAE, 42 joint blocks, and the three-stage optimizer and noise schedules. Appendix B covers pretraining data, with per-source record counts and an early filtering comparison that retains 43.35% of 1,183,622,445 source records. Appendix C covers caption and annotation recipes. Appendix D covers RoPE ablations and Appendix E covers convergence curves. Appendix F covers enhancer implementation. Appendices G and H cover benchmarks and rubric evaluations. Appendices I to K give qualitative cases, and Appendix L is the related-work discussion.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix gives the architecture, training, dataset, filtering, figure and related-work details behind the main text.
